theater: 幼發拉底河中游與巴比倫城

battle.name: 穆爾西里一世的行動
battle.theater: 幼發拉底河中游與巴比倫城
battle.brief: 公元前1650年前後，赫梯王穆爾西里一世率軍沿幼發拉底河南下，先取哈蘇瓦與阿勒頌，再深入美索不達米亞平原，於公元前1595年前後攻破巴比倫城，終結阿摩利特王朝。卡面的埃及長矛是同族的前身：早王朝的銅矛在兩千年間被同一套金屬矛頭配木桿的兵種延續，遠征的先鋒仍靠它結陣。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 穆爾西里一世的行動，是赫梯王國對美索不達米亞中游巴比倫尼亞的一系列遠征，戰爭列表把開端繫在公元前1650年前後，最後以公元前1595年洗劫巴比倫收尾。交戰的一方是赫梯：以安納托利亞高原的哈圖沙為都，王室自領一支常備步兵與車隊，外加弓手與投石手；其餘兵員由臣屬邦國分擔——西部的阿拉瓦集團、北部的卡斯基人部落、幼發拉底河上游的哈伊人，以及濱海諸城各自派出的分遣隊。指揮系統簡潔：戰略全由大王穆爾西里在行軍縱隊中決定，各分遣隊只負責本部的徵集、運輸與宿營，王室車隊擔當全軍的偵察與衝鋒，沒有留下可核對的幕僚名冊。另一方是巴比倫尼亞的城市聯盟，以巴比倫城為核心，末期阿摩利特王朝已四分五裂：各城互不信任，埃蘭、亞述與埃及在三方之間此消彼長，卡西特人是否已穩坐巴比倫王位仍有爭議。防守方倚仗尼布沙伊沙爾新建的高牆、伊什塔爾門與城防民兵，以及埃薩吉拉神廟的自衛武裝；但城邦聯盟沒有能與赫梯車兵正面競逐的野戰力量，這正是穆爾西里敢於深入平原的前提。
countriesEn: The campaigns of Muršili I were a series of Hittite expeditions against Babylonia in central Mesopotamia, whose opening the war lists place at around 1650 BC and whose climax was the sack of Babylon in about 1595 BC. One side was Hatti: a kingdom with its capital on the Anatolian plateau at Hattusa, where the crown kept a standing force of infantry and chariots backed by archers and slingers, while the rest of the manpower was provided by client states — the Arzawa confederation of western Anatolia, the Kaska tribes of the north, the Haya of the upper Euphrates, and detachments sent by the coastal cities. The command system was simple: strategy rested entirely with the Great King in the column of march; the detachments handled their own levying, transport and billeting; the royal chariot corps served as the army's scouts and shock troops, and no roster of staff officers survives. The other side was the city league of Babylonia, centred on Babylon, where the late Amorite dynasty had already come apart: the cities distrusted one another, Elam, Assyria and Egypt shifted their weight around the region in turn, and whether the Kassites had already settled on the Babylonian throne is still disputed. The defenders relied on the new walls raised by Nebuchadnezzar II, on the Ishtar Gate, on a city militia, and on the armed guards of the Esagila temple; yet the city league had nothing in the open field that could stand against Hittite chariots, and that was exactly the precondition for Muršili's descent into the plain.
people: 穆爾西里一世是赫梯的第四位王，約公元前1620年即位，父親哈圖西里一世開創的安納托利亞霸業在他手上轉為對外擴張。他的母親帕達提烏出身巴比倫的望族，赫梯的《解俘歌》正是藉這層關係，把進軍美索不達米亞說成回到母系祖地。兄弟皮塔納曾短期執掌王位，叔父哈尼爾與王室的其他成員在早期徵召中擔當統兵之責。巴比倫方面，末期阿摩利特王卡布齊伊爾在位到公元前1582年前後，其宮廷與埃薩吉拉神廟的書吏群是唯一留下當代記錄的人：一條巴比倫編年史殘片寫著赫梯國的國王來了、毀了巴比倫，另一塊出土於西帕爾神廟的泥板提到赫梯軍隊的破壞與神像被掠。匿名學者留下的《致神書》（第五塊 Tablet V 269）討論一次日蝕與赫梯王進軍所帶來的凶兆，試圖向神學讀者解釋王軍為何遲遲不能推進。赫梯方面的同期年表幾乎全毀，穆爾西里一世究竟如何統兵，只能從這些巴比倫方面的孤證，加上《解俘歌》的文體與用詞反推。
peopleEn: Muršili I was the fourth king of Hatti, taking the throne around 1620 BC; the Anatolian ascendancy begun by his father Hattusili I passed under him into open expansion. His mother Paddativu came from a Babylonian noble house, and the Hittite Song of Release uses precisely that connection to present the march into Mesopotamia as a return to the maternal homeland of the dynasty. His brother Pithana ruled for a short time, and his uncle Hanyer and other members of the royal family acted as commanders in the early levies. On the Babylonian side, the late Amorite king Kabzi-il ruled until about 1582 BC, and his palace together with the scribes of the Esagila temple produced the only contemporary record: a fragmentary Babylonian chronicle line stating that the king of the land of Hatti came and destroyed Babylon, and a tablet from the temple at Sippar that mentions destruction by the Hittite troops and the carrying off of divine images. An anonymous scholar left the Letter to the God, in which the fifth tablet discusses a solar eclipse and the ill omens attending the Hittite king's advance, trying to explain to a learned audience why the royal army could not push forward. Almost every Hittite annalist of the same age is lost, so how Muršili actually led his host can only be reconstructed from these Babylonian fragments together with the rhetoric of the Song of Release.
kits: 卡面是早王朝埃及的長矛：銅或青銅矛頭綁在木桿上，屬於先刺後砍的步兵通用裝備。赫梯遠征軍的骨幹兵種與它同源，公元前二千紀中葉的安納托利亞與敘利亞步兵以矛為主，葉形或柳葉形的銅矛頭套在木桿上，配一柄短彎刀、斧與一張圓盾，近身格鬥靠矛尖與斧背。弓對赫梯人是次要兵器，箭鏈多為骨或燧石，弓形與上弦方式在青銅時代已經定型；投石手更多見於游擊與守城。真正的打擊骨幹是雙馬雙輪的輕型戰車，車上三人：持盾者、持矛者與御者，車兵用矛而不是長槍。攻城需要撞槌、撞杆與可移動的攻城塔，還要靠河道船隻把攻城器材運抵城下。安納托利亞是當時主要的鐵礦區，赫梯王室的鐵匠行會造出刀、斧與矛頭，但大軍仍以青銅為主，鐵只配給近衛與工匠。安納托利亞與敘利亞出土的矛頭標本，無論形制還是綁法，都能在這件埃及早王朝長矛的技藝譜系中找到源頭：先造矛頭，再配木桿，兩千年不變。
kitsEn: The card shows the long spear of early dynastic Egypt: a copper or bronze head bound to a wooden shaft, part of the general infantry kit that thrusts first and cuts afterwards. The backbone of Muršili's army was of the same family. Anatolian and Syrian infantry of the mid second millennium fought principally with the spear, a leaf-shaped or willow-leaf copper head slipped onto a wooden shaft, accompanied by a short curved sword, an axe and a round shield, with the spear point and the back of the axe doing the work in close combat. The bow was a secondary arm for the Hittites, its arrowheads mostly bone or flint, with bow shape and string tension already fixed by the Bronze Age, while slingers appear more often in raiding and in the defence of walls. The real shock arm was the light two-horse, two-wheel chariot carrying three men — a shield bearer, a spear bearer and a driver — and the charioteers fought with spear rather than lance. Siege work required rams, battering poles and movable towers, and river craft had to carry that equipment to the walls. Anatolia was then the chief source of iron, and the royal Hittite smiths turned out blades, axes and spearheads, yet the mass of the army remained bronze-armed and iron went to the royal guard and to craftsmen. The spearheads excavated in Anatolia and Syria, in form and in binding alike, trace their pedigree to the technique of this early dynastic Egyptian spear: forge the head first, fit the shaft afterwards, and keep the practice unchanged for two thousand years.
tactics: 穆爾西里一世的戰術可以分三段。第一段是打通敘利亞的通道：先取哈蘇瓦，再取阿勒頌，沿幼發拉底河中游立住渡口與糧站，把安納托利亞與美索不達米亞之間的道路握在手裡。第二段是強渡幼發拉底河。哈圖西里一世留下的告誡是，敘利亞的道路狹窄多彎，敵人慣於設伏，車兵不可散開，行軍必須宿營在營地之內，車陣與步兵方陣之間要留出能互相支援的距離。第三段是進攻巴比倫本城：車兵負責壓制城外的游擊與襲擾，步兵結成長矛密集的方陣推向城門，攻城器材同時作業，必要時利用河道讓部隊沿水陸兩面同時接近；城破之後的縱掠、撤退與戰利品分配，由王室隨軍紀律維持，軍隊在河東的駐地待命，不把全部輜重帶走。整體而言，這是一場以車兵擔任偵察與衝鋒、以步兵作為攻堅主體、以安納托利亞為後方根基的深遠出擊，而不是一次就地的野戰。
tacticsEn: The tactics of Muršili's war fall into three stages. The first was to open the road through Syria: take Hassuwa first, then Alalakh, establish crossings and supply depots along the middle Euphrates, and hold the road between Anatolia and Mesopotamia in the palm of the hand. The second was the crossing of the Euphrates. Hattusili I left a standing warning: the roads of Syria are narrow and full of bends, the enemy lies in wait at every turn, the chariots must not scatter, the march must be spent inside the camp, and the chariots and the infantry squares must stand close enough to support one another. The third stage was the assault on Babylon itself. The chariots were tasked with pinning down the sorties and raids of the defenders outside the walls; the infantry closed into a dense spear square and pushed towards the gates; the siege equipment was worked at the same time, and the river was used where necessary so that troops could approach from the water side as well as the land. After the breach, the order of the sack, the withdrawal and the division of booty were kept by the royal discipline that travelled with the army, and the host stood ready in its camp east of the river rather than carrying off all its baggage. In the whole, this was a deep sortie that used chariots for scouting and shock, infantry for the assault, and Anatolia as its base, not a battle fought on the spot.
data: 可核對的數字非常有限，這本身就是這場戰爭的特徵。穆爾西里一世在位約公元前1620至1590年；戰爭列表把行動繫在公元前1650年前後，學界通常把洗劫巴比倫定在公元前1595年。從哈圖沙到巴比倫，直線距離約八百公里，沿幼發拉底河谷的行軍路線超過一千公里，車隊的實際行程還要加上在敘利亞的停留。巴比倫城牆內的面積約四百公頃，牆厚可達八米、牆高約十八米，設八座城門；希羅多德記載牆高八十英尺、周長近五十華里，數字明顯被誇大，考古實測才是準繩。公元前1595年6月2日的一次日蝕，是《致神書》提及的那次天象，本卡所記的月份即依此推定。卡西特王朝自此上位，統治巴比倫約四百四十年、共三十五位君王，終於公元前1155年亡於埃蘭。赫梯遠征軍的兵力數字沒有留下來：穆爾西里的年表已失，巴比倫編年史只有一句話。能作旁證的只有更晚的赫梯資料，例如王室敕令殘片要求城鎮按住戶徵發民兵，武器包括弓、矛、短劍、斧與盾；又如公元前十三世紀卡迭石之戰的編年，記下赫梯方投入數千輛戰車——那是同一國家在鼎盛期的規模，不是這次遠征的數字。
dataEn: The verifiable figures are extremely few, and that scarcity is itself a feature of this war. Muršili I reigned from roughly 1620 to 1590 BC. The war lists attach the campaigns to around 1650 BC, while scholarship usually fixes the sack of Babylon in 1595 BC. From Hattusa to Babylon the straight line is about eight hundred kilometres, and the marching route down the Euphrates valley runs past a thousand; the chariots' actual progress was longer still, once the halts in Syria are added. The area inside the walls of Babylon was about four hundred hectares; the walls reach eight metres thick and roughly eighteen metres high and had eight gates. Herodotus gives a height of eighty feet and a circuit approaching fifty miles, figures plainly exaggerated, and the excavated masonry is the only trustworthy measure. A solar eclipse on 2 June 1595 BC is the phenomenon mentioned in the Letter to the God, and the month recorded on this card follows that dating. From then on the Kassite dynasty sat on the Babylonian throne, ruling Babylonia for about four hundred and forty years through thirty-five kings, and finally perishing at the hands of Elam in 1155 BC. No figure survives for the size of Muršili's expeditionary force: his annals are lost and the Babylonian chronicle preserves a single sentence. Only later Hittite material can serve as an indirect check — fragments of royal ordinances that require towns to levy militia by household, armed with bow, spear, short sword, axe and shield, and the annals of the battle of Kadesh in the thirteenth century BC, which record thousands of Hittite chariots. That is the scale of the same state at its height, not a number belonging to this campaign.
cause: 打起來的原因有三層。最表層是赫梯王權本身：穆爾西里一世在哈圖西里一世死後面對王位競爭與邊境叛亂，需要一次能震懾全境的大勝，年輕的王用遠征來建立自己的威望。中層是地理與經濟：安納托利亞出鐵、錫與林材，美索不達米亞出穀物、鹽與織物，兩地之間的幼發拉底河谷商路是赫梯王國財政的命脈；掌握巴比倫一線，就等於插進埃蘭與亞述之間，取得對兩河流域貿易的仲裁權。最深的一層是王室的法統宣稱：穆爾西里的母親出自巴比倫，赫梯文本藉此把進軍說成收回母系祖地，把一場征服包裝成復國。時局也提供了窗口：末期阿摩利特王朝的諸王互相爭奪，埃及在敘利亞的介入已隨圖特摩斯三世的遠征轉為守勢，阿卡德王國的舊秩序崩解後留下真空，赫梯此前又在哈蘇瓦與阿勒頌得手，敘利亞的城邦已習慣向赫梯求助，於是遠征順理成章。
causeEn: Three layers of reason lie behind the fighting. At the surface is Hittite kingship itself: after the death of Hattusili I, Muršili I faced rivals for the throne and revolts along the frontier, and needed a blow that would overawe the whole country; a young king built his authority on a distant campaign. Beneath that lie geography and economics: Anatolia produced iron, tin and timber, Mesopotamia produced grain, salt and woven cloth, and the trading roads of the Euphrates valley between them were the life of the Hittite treasury. Holding the Babylonian line meant driving a wedge between Elam and Assyria and taking on the right to arbitrate the trade of the Euphrates. At the deepest level sits a claim of dynastic legitimacy: Muršili's mother was Babylonian, and the Hittite texts use that fact to present the advance as the recovery of the maternal homeland, dressing conquest up as restoration. The moment also offered its window. The late Amorite kings quarrelled with one another, Egyptian intervention in Syria had already turned defensive after the campaigns of Thutmose III, the collapse of the old Akkadian order had left a vacuum, and the Hittites had already taken Hassuwa and Alalakh, so that the Syrian cities had grown used to calling on Hatti for help. The expedition followed naturally from all of this.
impact: 結果的重量遠超過一場攻城。巴比倫第一次淪陷，末期阿摩利特王朝斷裂，卡西特人坐上王位，此後四百四十年巴比倫尼亞不再獨自當家；這道裂縫也把埃蘭與亞述推到重新瓜分兩河流域的位置上。對赫梯而言，這是從王國走向帝國的分水嶺：敘利亞的城邦第一次被一個安納托利亞政體納編，赫梯王成為遠方城邦求援的對象，也把巴比倫的泥板、宮廷禮制與神學文本帶回哈圖沙，安納托利亞與美索不達米亞之間的器物、工藝與信仰從此不再隔絕。此後數百年，巴比倫人把赫梯視為北方最兇惡的來客；但赫梯自己也沒有因此建立常駐的統治機構，這次打擊留下的不是征服而是創傷——城市的宮殿、神廟與財富被搬空，供水與耕種系統受損，數十年後的巴比倫仍要從廢墟中重新站起來。至於史料，這場戰爭幾乎沒有留下正面記載：赫梯一方的年表全毀，我們所知的絕大部分來自巴比倫方面的孤證殘片；而巴比倫城的考古發掘自十九世紀末以來雖已系統進行，至今仍未找到足以對應這次洗劫的決定性戰場層位。
impactEn: The consequences reached far beyond the walls that were breached. Babylon fell for the first time, the late Amorite dynasty was broken, and the Kassites took the throne, so that for four hundred and forty years Babylonia no longer ruled itself; the same fissure pushed Elam and Assyria into positions where they could once again divide the Euphrates region between them. For the Hittites this was the watershed between kingdom and empire. The Syrian cities were for the first time enrolled in the system of an Anatolian power, the Hittite king became the appeal of distant towns, and the tablets, court ritual and theological texts of Babylon travelled back to Hattusa, so that objects, craft and belief between Anatolia and Mesopotamia were no longer sealed off from one another. For centuries afterwards the Babylonians counted the Hittites among the most unwelcome visitors from the north. Yet Hatti itself built no standing administration in the wake of the blow, and what the raid left behind was trauma rather than rule: the palaces, temples and wealth of the city were carried off, the water supply and the cultivated land were damaged, and Babylonia had to stand up again from the ruins decades later. As for the record, this war left almost no direct testimony: the Hittite annals are gone, and nearly everything we know comes from a handful of Babylonian fragments. Systematic excavation at Babylon has been under way since the end of the nineteenth century, yet no decisive battlefield layer corresponding to this sack has been identified.
result: 公元前1595年，巴比倫陷落。宮殿與神廟遭掠，瑪爾杜克神像被帶往哈圖沙——這尊像後來在埃蘭人手中輾轉，直到公元前六世紀巴比倫尼亞復國時才被迎回都城。巴比倫王位上的阿摩利特王朝就此終結，赫梯的遠征軍在劫掠後撤回安納托利亞，穆爾西里一世獲得大王的威望，赫梯對敘利亞與幼發拉底河中游的支配也鞏固下來。但遠征沒有帶來常駐的官吏、沒有帶來稅賦、也沒有帶來新的行省：巴比倫很快恢復原狀，卡西特人接手了這座殘破但仍富庶的城，兩河流域進入了漫長的卡西特時期。穆爾西里一世大約在公元前1590年去世，赫梯隨即陷入王位繼承的混亂，先前的攻勢為之中斷；直到公元前十五世紀，赫梯才重新集結力量，與米坦尼、埃及其他勢力在敘利亞長期角力。就這場戰爭本身而言，可以確定的是：遠征成功、攻城成功、王朝更替成功，而隨後的統治失敗。由於赫梯方面的同期記錄幾乎全毀，遠征的具體路線、兵員編制與攻城細節只能從巴比倫方面的斷簡殘片與後世學者的推斷重建，本卡所述的月份與若干部署即屬此類推斷。
resultEn: In 1595 BC Babylon fell. The palaces and the temples were plundered and the statue of Marduk was carried off to Hattusa; that statue later passed through Elamite hands and was not brought back to its city until the Neo-Babylonian restoration of the sixth century BC. The Amorite dynasty on the Babylonian throne ended there and then, the Hittite expedition withdrew to Anatolia after the sack, Muršili I acquired the standing of a Great King, and Hittite ascendancy over Syria and the middle Euphrates was consolidated. But the expedition brought no resident officials, no new taxes and no new province. Babylon soon returned to its old shape, the Kassites took over a city that was ruined yet still rich, and the Euphrates region entered the long Kassite period. Muršili I died around 1590 BC, Hatti fell into a struggle over the succession, and the earlier momentum was broken; only in the fifteenth century BC did the Hittites rally again to contend with Mitanni, Elam and other powers in Syria for the long run. As for this war itself, what can be settled is that the expedition succeeded, the siege succeeded and the dynastic change succeeded, while the subsequent governance failed. Because nearly all Hittite contemporary record is lost, the exact route of the march, the composition of the host and the details of the siege can only be rebuilt from the broken Babylonian fragments and from the reconstructions of later scholars; the month given on this card and several of the deployments described above belong to that class of inference.
